scoreJustification:
The 9router system is NOT production-ready. Key critical gaps:

1. Circuit breaker service exists but is NOT integrated into the request pipeline - providers can cascade failures without any protection mechanism. This is the most critical reliability gap.

2. No metrics endpoint exists - operators have zero way to query system state, error rates, or latency distributions. This violates fundamental SRE practices.

3. In-memory state (_pendingRequests, _lastErrorProvider, _recentRing) resets on process restart - after a deploy or crash, all pending request tracking and error state is lost, forcing a "cold start" period where the system is blind.

4. No deployment-time SLO validation gate - there is no mechanism to prevent deployments when error budgets are near exhaustion.

5. Health check endpoint only confirms the HTTP server is running, not that the SSE pipeline, circuit breakers, or account status is healthy.

6. No structured JSON logs with request ID, model, provider, status, latency - makes debugging production incidents extremely difficult.

7. No chaos engineering test suite - no confidence in system behavior under failure conditions.

The system scores 45/100 because: core functionality works well, pattern matching is correct, RTK strict mode is properly implemented, and the drift prevention framework is documented. However, the critical production readiness gaps (observability, reliability, and operational control) are significant and would prevent a responsible SRE from approving this system for production use without substantial remediation.

items.title: Integrate circuit breaker into request pipeline
items.description: Wire getCircuitBreaker() calls in handlers/executors before upstream API calls. Record failures on errors, record successes on completion. Enable per-provider circuit breaker configurations via CIRCUIT_BREAKER_CONFIG.providers.
items.technicalDebtReference: SRE_ADR.md gap: "no circuit breaker for consistently failing providers"
items.verification: After integration, verify that consistently failing providers get circuit breaker OPEN state and requests are rejected with 503 before exhausting all accounts.

items.title: Implement Prometheus metrics endpoint /metrics
items.description: Add endpoint that exposes: sse_requests_total (count, by status, by provider, by endpoint), sse_request_latency_seconds (histogram: p50, p95, p99), sse_pending_requests (gauge by model/provider), sse_active_accounts (gauge by provider), sse_error_budget_consumed (gauge 0-1).
items.verification: After implementation, curl /metrics should return valid metric lines that can be scraped by Prometheus.

items.title: Persist in-memory state on process restart
items.description: Add shutdown hook (process 'beforeunload' or SIGTERM) that saves _pendingRequests, _lastErrorProvider, _recentRing to SQLite/lowdb. On startup, load persisted state. This ensures pending request tracking and error state survive deploys and crashes.
items.technicalDebtReference: SRE_ADR.md Section 3.2: "In-memory state volatility" - "Persist in-memory state to DB on shutdown"
items.verification: After restart, verify that _pendingRequests and _lastErrorProvider are preserved from before shutdown.

items.title: Enhance health check endpoint with pipeline status
items.description: Extend /api/health to return: SSE handler status (initialized), pending request count, error budget remaining (percentage), active accounts per provider, circuit breaker states for key providers. Keep the existing {ok: true} as a minimum but add substantial operational data.
items.technicalDebtReference: SRE_ADR.md Section 3.2: "No health check endpoint" - recommended: returning SSE handler status, pending count, error budget, active accounts
items.verification: After enhancement, curl /api/health should return JSON with fields: status, pendingRequests, errorBudget, activeAccounts, circuitBreakers (partial).

items.title: Add structured JSON logging with request ID, model, provider, status, latency
items.description: Enhance the logger to emit structured JSON entries containing: requestId, provider, model, status, latencyMs, endpoint, timestamp. Ensure correlation across the full pipeline (chatCore → translator → executor → response). Mask sensitive data (API keys) in structured output.
items.technicalDebtReference: SRE_ADR.md Section 8.4: "Add structured JSON logs with request ID, model, provider, status, latency"
items.verification: After implementation, log entries should be parseable JSON with the specified fields, and request IDs should be traceable across the full request lifecycle.

items.title: Implement deployment-time SLO validation gate
items.description: Create a deployment gate/check that validates the error budget won't be exceeded. If consuming >10% of error budget, block deployment or require canary-first approach. Integrate with CI/CD pipeline.
items.technicalDebtReference: SRE_ADR.md Section 4.3: "Canary deployments with SLO monitoring before full rollout" and "SLO gate in deployment pipeline"
items.verification: After implementation, attempt a deployment when error budget is <10% remaining should fail the deployment gate or require canary flag.

items.title: Implement full SLO/SLI tracking
items.description: Track TTS success rate (target 99.9%), chat completion success rate (target 99.8%), stream continuity rate (target 99.5%). Implement SLIs and tie to error budget calculations. 30-day windows with burn rate alerts.
items.technicalDebtReference: SRE_ADR.md Section 5: SLO/SLI Definitions - current SLI implementation status shows gaps in TTS, chat, and stream success rates
items.verification: After implementation, getUsageStats() or /metrics should include TTS success rate, chat completion success rate, and stream completion rate with 30-day windows.

items.title: Create chaos engineering test suite
items.description: Scripted failure injection tests for key failure modes: account kill switch (mark all accounts unavailable), latency spike (inject delay), translator corruption (malformed bodies), provider timeout (block upstream). Measure MTTR, fallback success rate, error budget impact.

items.verification: After implementation, run chaos tests and verify that fallback behaviors (circuit breaker, account marking, RTK fail-open) work as expected under injected failures.

items.title: Make RTK strict mode operationally practical
